prompt.context: Your client is a company which has experienced growth in the past through acquisition. It is composed of the following areas: (1) Automotive parts division #1 — has three different areas within the division; (2) Construction materials division; (3) Automotive parts division #3 — owns four separate companies.
prompt.question: Identify consolidation and off-shoring opportunities for this company.

clarifying_info.q: What does Auto parts division #1 produce and who are its customers?
clarifying_info.a: Auto parts division #1 produces metallic parts and sells to OEMs.

clarifying_info.q: What does the Construction materials division produce and who are its customers?
clarifying_info.a: It produces plumbing, electrical, and other building materials. Its customers are construction companies.

clarifying_info.q: What does Auto parts division #3 produce and who are its customers?
clarifying_info.a: Auto parts division #3 produces rubber parts and sells to OEMs.

clarifying_info.q: Does the company operate any call centers?
clarifying_info.a: No, the company does not operate any call centers.

clarifying_info.q: How do the auto businesses distribute their products?
clarifying_info.a: Auto businesses ship directly from their plants to customer plants — there are no warehouses.

framework: Cost — tailor to specific industries: SG&A, PPE, Purchasing, Other Operational (Distribution, Design Services, Best Practices)
Identify levels at which consolidation can occur (across subsidiaries within a division, across divisions, offshore)

questions.prompt: What are the SG&A consolidation and off-shoring opportunities?
questions.guidance: Sales forces across both automotive divisions should be consolidated under a central director to share best practices; sales reps should cover all rubber companies rather than maintaining individual reps per subsidiary. G&A functions (Accounting, Billing, Finance) should be consolidated to reduce cost and improve quality. Billing, some accounting, and some finance can be offshored to India — common across industries and should not be difficult to accomplish.

questions.prompt: What are the PPE (plant, property, equipment) consolidation opportunities?
questions.guidance: Consolidating SG&A allows combining some or all headquarters. Utilization should be reviewed to find opportunities to consolidate manufacturing and design capacity at high utilization levels (balanced against growth plans). Main areas: across metallic auto companies, across rubber auto companies, and potentially minor overlap between metallic auto and construction. Footprint rationalization should be balanced against customer locations/distribution needs and manufacturing costs — significant opportunity to shift manufacturing to China.

questions.prompt: What are the Purchasing consolidation opportunities?
questions.guidance: Purchasing must be centralized to maximize buyer power across all three divisions and reduce headcount. Centralization is critical given that both auto divisions sell to OEMs and likely share raw material categories.

questions.prompt: What are the Distribution and Design Services opportunities?
questions.guidance: Distribution: Main opportunities are between the two auto divisions since they share OEM customers. A consolidated distribution network may offer substantial savings on trucking/shipping. Design Services: Consolidate design within each auto area and share best practices across both. Offshore computer-aided design and lower-level engineering work — this should save approximately 50% where applied and can also improve cycle time because teams will work around the clock across time zones.

math.setup: Offshore design services saves ~50% of design costs where applied.
steps: Identify total design services spend across both auto divisions
Apply 50% savings rate to the offshored portion
math.answer: ~50% cost reduction on offshored design services

questions.prompt: What are the Revenue / Cross-selling opportunities?
questions.guidance: A central director over both auto divisions will help the sales team leverage contacts across areas. The candidate should recognize the risk of going to OEMs as a central integrated supplier: integrated solutions have been popular with OEMs but suppliers are typically less profitable in those arrangements and become bigger targets for price givebacks. Recommendation: keep separate rubber and metallic salespeople and products, but leverage the shared network and best practices — effectively an in-house manufacturer's representative model.
